publication: Second Quarter Health Insurance Segment Profitability Trends
scope: individual medical, MFA's own estimate (includes territories and CHIP-in-individual; no annual-filer adjustment)
notes: KFF's 20.5M uses a narrower definition; KFF (2026-10-14) attributes the difference to medical-focus plans only, excluding territories, CHIP adjustment and annual-filer adjustment. MFA 26.5M→21.9M = −17.4%, consistent with KFF's citation of MFA's −17.2%. Second MFA vintage: MFA's Sep 29, 2026 brief "Second Quarter Health Insurance Enrollment Trends: Market Segment Performance" reports Individual membership "for both on-and-off the marketplace exchanges" of 22 million (−17.2% from 26.5 million); KFF's cited −17.2% is that brief's figure, not a match to this row's 21.9M. Definitions as each brief states them: this Oct 28 brief's 21.9M is "individual medical plans" from NAIC financial statements and MFA estimates, and its analysis data come from the NAIC Quarterly Exhibit of Premiums, Enrollment & Utilization (about 80% of the market; California HMO plans not reporting to the NAIC and some other plans do not file it); the Sep 29 brief's 22M is Health Coverage Portal segment membership from NAIC, CA DMHC, CMS and state agency filings, covering carriers with business in the U.S. and U.S. territories, where some carriers' individual membership may include CHIP. Neither brief explains the 0.1M difference; not reconciled here. Note: the territories/CHIP language in this row's scope label appears in the Sep 29 brief's About the Data, not in the Oct 28 brief.
